original_question: For the hypergraphic planted clique (HPC) detection problem, where one must distinguish an Erdős-Rényi d-hypergraph G_d(N, 1/2) from a planted-clique alternative G_d(N, 1/2, κ) formed by choosing κ vertices uniformly at random and connecting every hyperedge whose vertices all lie in that planted set, what is the sharp threshold on the clique size κ at which polynomial-time singular-value-decomposition-based detection on a matricization or unfolding of the adjacency tensor succeeds, and is there some other polynomial-time algorithm that can solve HPC detection for κ below that SVD threshold?
target_in_paper: Section 3, Challenge 1, read together with the Section 2 definition of HPC detection in equation (1), the definition of the adjacency tensor A=A(G), and the Section 2 discussion immediately preceding Conjecture 1 that records the currently known SVD success/failure regime.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper’s actual open problem as the two-part Question in Section 3, Challenge 1: determine the SVD-based detection limit for hypergraphic planted clique after matricizing/unfolding the adjacency tensor, and ask whether any polynomial-time algorithm can succeed for smaller clique size. It also correctly states the null/alternative models G_d(N,1/2) versus G_d(N,1/2,κ) and the planted-set construction.
missing_details: The paper is asymptotic in N, so the question should explicitly say that N→∞.
The order d should be fixed. In the surrounding HPC discussion the intended hypergraph case is d≥3, while Conjecture 1 is stated for any fixed d≥2.
The object being unfolded is specifically the adjacency tensor A=A(G)∈{0,1}^{N⊗d}, with A_{i1,...,id}=1 iff {i1,...,id} is a hyperedge and 0 otherwise.
Under H1, the planted set K is chosen uniformly at random among all κ-subsets of [N], and every d-hyperedge contained entirely in K is added.
The success criterion should be stated: a sequence of polynomial-time tests φ_N solves detection if P_H0(φ_N(G)=1)+P_H1(φ_N(G)=0)→0.
The paper’s wording is 'the sharp limit of κ' for SVD on a matricization/unfolding of A, not a broader computational threshold for HPC as a whole.
To be paper-faithful, the question should mention the known baseline motivating the challenge: SVD is known to solve HPC when κ=Ω(√N) and to fail when κ=N^{1/2-ε} for any ε>0.
The second part asks for any other polynomial-time algorithm below the SVD limit, not specifically another spectral or tensor-unfolding method.
No ambient field/ring, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency assumptions are involved here; the relevant objects are {0,1}-valued adjacency tensors of d-uniform hypergraphs.
refined_question: For a fixed integer d≥3, let G be a d-uniform hypergraph on [N], let A=A(G)∈{0,1}^{N⊗d} be its adjacency tensor, and consider the hypergraphic planted clique detection problem with hypotheses H0:G∼G_d(N,1/2) versus H1:G∼G_d(N,1/2,κ), where under H1 a set K⊂[N] of size κ is chosen uniformly at random and every d-hyperedge contained in K is planted; a sequence of polynomial-time tests solves detection if P_H0(φ_N(G)=1)+P_H1(φ_N(G)=0)→0 as N→∞. What is the sharp asymptotic limit of κ for which applying singular value decomposition to a matricization/unfolding of A guarantees successful HPC detection, and does there exist any polynomial-time algorithm that solves HPC detection for κ asymptotically below that SVD limit?
justification: The draft is aimed at Section 3, Challenge 1, not at the paper’s main hardness conjecture or its PC-vs-HPC reduction question. The match is very close because your two clauses mirror the two sentences of Challenge 1 almost verbatim. To make it fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper, one must import the Section 2 model definition, the adjacency-tensor notation, the asymptotic error criterion for detection, and the fixed-d assumption. This short COLT note contains Section 2, equation (1), Conjecture 1, and Challenges 1–3, but no Proposition 1.2 or Theorem 1.3; the nearest official formulation for your draft is therefore Section 3, Challenge 1, with notation supplied by Section 2.
